decision_reason: VIVODEPOT is a current personal-data wallet product of private Vivodepot GmbH, not software created, commissioned, funded, sponsored, or stewarded by a government agency. Its xShare/EU-program relationship is an evaluation/integration lead rather than evidence that an agency originated this product. I verified the live canonical source, the exact EUPL-1.2 scope, 2026 grant-bearing source commit, and current Beta 16 distribution separately; no qualifying independent deployment/use pathway was established. The assigned GitHub URL currently returns 404, and the official site points to the publicly cloneable OpenCode repository. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The first-party About page identifies Vivodepot as a product of Vivodepot GmbH in Berlin. Its xShare page describes participation/evaluation, not government commissioning or funding of the product itself; use of government-issued templates also does not establish provenance.

public_source.note: The assigned github.com/carolaklessen/vivodepot URL returns 404, but Vivodepot's official site links its source to OpenCode and the canonical repository is publicly cloneable at this OpenCode path (the old assigned path redirects to it).

eligible_license.note: The root EUPL-1.2 grant and the first-party licensing policy cover the application, reader, module generator, test suite, tools, and author-written documentation/templates. Third-party official government form text is expressly excluded; unrelated templates/marks are not treated as code grants. EUPL-1.2 is OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The official site documents a current Beta 16 one-file download and user instructions. The separate xShare relationship is described inconsistently across first-party pages (selected/testing versus an expression of interest pending consortium acceptance), and I found no independent deployment/reuse proof meeting the intake notability pathway.

product_identity: VIVODEPOT, an offline, single-file personal-data/document wallet
agency: No government-originating agency identified; developed and sold by Vivodepot GmbH. The EU xShare consortium is described as a prospective test/integration relationship, not the product originator.
geography: Berlin, Germany (Vivodepot GmbH); no sponsoring-government geography established
license: EUPL-1.2 for first-party application/tooling and author-written documentation/templates; third-party official government wording is excluded by LICENSING.md
status_note: The current OpenCode source's first observed grant-bearing commit is 2026-09-27 (the assigned GitHub URL is 404); current official download is Beta 16. The official site distinguishes EUPL-1.2 application code from a time-delayed BUSL-to-EUPL template handover mechanism, but LICENSING.md says the public repository's first-party software scope is EUPL-1.2. Government forms embedded as content are not Vivodepot software provenance. No exact GOSDIR catalog duplicate found.

decision_reason: TagliandOnline is a municipal software product: its first-party publiccode.yml names Comune di Castagneto Carducci as the organization and user, gives municipal IT/innovation-office maintainers and municipal email contacts, and the city documents that office's software-development remit. The code is public and the root grant is AGPL-3.0-or-later, with a 2025 first licensed-source commit. However, I could not independently verify a municipality product/service page, deployed instance, or actual operational use. Although version tags and install/user docs exist, the manifest's self-reported user/owner claims are not enough by themselves to clear the primary-evidence/notability baseline; hold for direct official service/use evidence.

government_provenance.note: The product's own publiccode.yml identifies the Comune di Castagneto Carducci as publisher and user and names its Ufficio Informatica e Innovazione and a municipal-email maintainer; the city's official PIAO independently confirms the office's remit includes developing/updating software. Attribution is to this specific municipal product, not inferred from a catalog label.

public_source.note: The assigned repository is the public application source, including frontend, backend, documentation, setup files, and version tags; Docker installation instructions are provided.

eligible_license.note: The first-party publiccode manifest declares AGPL-3.0-or-later, and the repository carries the corresponding GNU Affero GPL v3 text. This grant covers the TagliandOnline application source in this repository; it does not extend to third-party dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: The source provides a usable v0.3.2 tagged beta plus installation and user documentation, but I found no direct municipal page for the service or independent operational-use evidence. Publiccode's usedBy claim is self-reported and remains uncorroborated; hold pending direct official service/use evidence or an independently verifiable agency-published release record.

product_identity: TagliandOnline, a web/PWA municipal parking-permit and voucher-management application with document generation, applications, and field inspections
agency: Comune di Castagneto Carducci, specifically its Ufficio Informatica e Innovazione; first-party publiccode.yml attributes the product to the municipality
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later for the application source in this repository; external libraries retain their own licenses
status_note: The first repository commit containing the licensed application is 2025-12-30; metadata creation/retrieval dates are not used as the source year. Current source is non-archived and has v0.2.1–v0.3.2 version tags, Docker/setup instructions, and topic-specific user guides. Nonetheless, independent official evidence of production use or a municipal service URL was not found; the manifest's self-reported usedBy field remains uncorroborated. No exact catalog duplicate found.

decision_reason: Cboard is an AAC web application whose development was supported by UNICEF's Innovation Fund. I verified the publicly accessible canonical browser-client source, exact GPL-3.0-only code grant and separately licensed symbol content, the 2017 initial public GPL-identified source commit, current product availability/source activity, and UNICEF-documented deployments/pilots with children and professionals. The Cboard API is a separate repository and is not included in the client grant attribution here. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: UNICEF's Office of Innovation states that its Innovation Fund supported CIREHA and documents Cboard as the open-source AAC product developed/field-tested through that funded relationship. CIREHA is a private Argentine company; UNICEF is the product-specific public-international sponsor, not the application's sole author.

public_source.note: This public repository contains the browser/PWA application, user-facing functionality and development source. The project points to a live application at app.cboard.io. The related cboard-api backend is a separate public repository, not assumed to be covered solely by this repository's grant.

eligible_license.note: The current root license and README identify the application code as GNU GPL version 3 only (GPL-3.0-only; OSI-approved). The README separately attributes Mulberry symbols to CC BY-SA 4.0 and ARASAAC symbols to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; those non-code assets are not treated as GPL code. The sibling cboard-api has a separate grant.

primary_evidence.note: UNICEF documents the Cboard AAC application in an ECARO pilot involving children and more than 70 professionals across Croatia, Montenegro and Serbia; its current project website continues to offer the app and the source has recent code activity. This is product-specific operational/pilot use and current distribution, not merely the DPG catalog record.

product_identity: Cboard, an augmentative and alternative communication browser application/PWA using symbols and text-to-speech
agency: UNICEF Office of Innovation / UNICEF Innovation Fund (United Nations public-international organization); product developed by CIREHA, an Argentine AAC company, with UNICEF fund support
geography: CIREHA, Argentina; UNICEF-supported pilots in Croatia, Montenegro, and Serbia
license: GPL-3.0-only for the browser application code; symbol assets have separately identified CC BY-SA 4.0 and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 grants; the cboard-api backend is a separate repository
status_note: The 2017-08-03 initial public source commit by Shay Cojocaru includes an explicit README statement that code is GPLv3; current root LICENSE.txt and funding.json delimit it as GPL-3.0-only. The project remains active and its website currently links users to the application. The assignment is the browser client; the separate cboard-api backend and separately licensed symbol libraries are not silently folded into its code grant. No exact GOSDIR catalog duplicate found.

decision_reason: ICE is a government-funded immunization forecasting service, but the exact first public licensed-source year remains unresolved. NYC DOHMH documents its funding and operational use, the current repository carries the NYC copyright and LGPL-3.0-or-later grant, and current IHS installation documentation plus recent releases establish active operational availability. Official project records describe ICE as open source at conferences in 2012, whereas the earliest grant-bearing code commit I verified in the current public repository dates to 2016; the archived original Bitbucket distribution/history is needed to establish the first public licensed source year.

government_provenance.note: HLN's first-party project history states that ICE and related tools were originally developed with funding from New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, which retained copyright and released the software under LGPL. This establishes product-specific government funding; HLN's later contributions are distinguished from the city's originating sponsorship.

public_source.note: The assigned repository is the live public ICE web-service source with source/build/test files, versioned releases, Docker and standalone/Tomcat installation guidance. The project says it is bundled with OpenCDS libraries; their separate components and dependencies retain their own terms.

eligible_license.note: The repository's current License section grants GNU LGPL version 3 or any later version (LGPL-3.0-or-later) to ICE code; README identifies NYC DOHMH as copyright owner and HLN Consulting contributions. This is OSI-approved. Bundled OpenCDS and third-party dependencies are separate scopes.

primary_evidence.note: The Indian Health Service's November 2025 installation instructions document ICE as the operational forecast service used by its Resource and Patient Management System. NYC's 2023 algorithmic-tools report also identifies ICE in Bureau of Immunization patient forecasting; HLN released ICE 2.58.1 on 2026-08-18.

product_identity: Immunization Calculation Engine (ICE), an immunization evaluation and forecasting clinical decision-support service
agency: New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH), Bureau of Immunization; developed under NYC funding with HLN Consulting contributions. Indian Health Service is a documented operational downstream user.
geography: New York City, New York, United States (originating agency); Indian Health Service deployment is United States-wide
license: LGPL-3.0-or-later for ICE code under the NYC grant; bundled OpenCDS libraries and other dependencies remain separately licensed
status_note: Hold only on the exact public licensed-source year. Current public Git history shows the first verified LICENSE-header grant-bearing code commit in 2016, while the official project presentation index records open-source ICE presentations beginning in 2012; the current GitHub repo was created in 2019 and that repository metadata is not treated as source year. Need the original Bitbucket source history/release or another dated grant-bearing source artifact to confirm which date marks the first public licensed source. The other four-check evidence is strong and current. No exact catalog duplicate found.

decision_reason: Ceph is an open-source distributed storage product that began as a UCSC research system under product-specific funding from the U.S. Department of Energy/NNSA Advanced Simulation and Computing program and national laboratories. The assigned organization URL resolves to a multi-repository org; I scoped this review to the core ceph/ceph distribution and recorded its per-file licensing exceptions. Current releases, installation docs, and Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre's production 11PB/27PB clusters establish a significant maintained product. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The UCSC Storage Systems Research Center page describes its Ceph prototype/source and lists Department of Energy/NNSA, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Sandia National Laboratories, and NSF among project sponsors. The Ceph Foundation history independently states that Ceph began in a national-laboratory-funded effort; this is product-origin funding, not merely later government use.

public_source.note: The assigned https://github.com/ceph URL is an organization with many independent repositories; the canonical core distributed-storage product source is github.com/ceph/ceph. It is public and active, with build and test material and versioned release history. Review does not automatically include Ceph CSI, Rook, or other sibling projects.

eligible_license.note: The core source README states that most Ceph code is distributed under LGPL 2.1 or LGPL 3.0; COPYING enumerates file-specific terms. These are OSI-approved LGPL grants. Some headers/code use GPL, BSD-style or public-domain terms, and docs use CC BY-SA-3.0; the SILL's single LGPL-2.1-only claim is too narrow and is not treated as a uniform grant over every file.

primary_evidence.note: A Ceph case study coauthored by Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre staff documents two production Ceph clusters: 11 PB for general research and 27 PB for radio astronomy. Current 2026 stable releases and official installation/user documentation support ongoing distribution.

product_identity: Ceph, the distributed object, block, and file storage system in the core ceph/ceph source repository
agency: U.S. Department of Energy/NNSA Advanced Simulation and Computing program through Lawrence Livermore, Los Alamos, and Sandia National Laboratories; research developed at the University of California, Santa Cruz
geography: United States (UC Santa Cruz and DOE/NNSA national laboratories)
license: Core Ceph source is mostly LGPL-2.1 or LGPL-3.0; see COPYING for file-specific GPL, BSD-style, public-domain, and documentation exceptions
status_note: Ceph's official history distinguishes code written in 2004, the project going public under LGPL in 2006, later DreamHost commercialization, and current community governance. The repository URL supplied to SILL is only an organization page; this review maps to the canonical core product repository. Current Ceph is not uniformly LGPL-2.1-only: COPYING lists file-specific grants and exceptions, and the README says most core code is LGPL 2.1 or 3.0. No exact catalog match found.
